html:
A noble of the Arverni of central Gaul who united the Gauls in a great revolt against Julius Caesar in 52 BCE.

His father Celtillus had been killed by his own people for trying to make himself king. Early in 52 BCE, while Caesar was away in Italy, Vercingetorix raised the Arverni and won over most of the tribes of Gaul. He had them burn their own towns and farms so Caesar's army could not feed itself, and he beat Caesar at the Battle of Gergovia, one of Caesar's few defeats.

Then he made a mistake. He shut his army into the hill town of Alesia, and Caesar walled it in (see Siege of Alesia). When a huge Gallic relief army failed to break through, Vercingetorix gave himself up. He was kept prisoner in Rome for six years, shown in Caesar's triumph in 46 BCE, and then put to death.

We know him almost only from Caesar's own account, the Gallic War. In the 1800s he became a French national hero; Napoleon III had a giant statue of him put up at Alesia in 1865. He also stands for the Celtic world that the Gallic Wars ended.
